design.heading: Design
design.text:
What c0250 builds on: c0117's dispatcher and chain (`dispatch.luau`, `dispatcher.luau`), c0256's exchange as redesigned (#323, prepared, before c0250: `.cache/dispatch/<id>/exchange/NNN-question.md` and `NNN-answer.md`, the re-run prompt that names the answer), #318 and #330's z-work (`work.luau`, `workread.luau`, `readycheck.luau`, `readyfacts.luau`), c0263's record (`provenance.md`, `provenance.record`, the `unblocked` event, the live actor), c0283's agent markers (`provenance.AGENT_VARS`, `provenance.hint`), c0248's stack (`done --through`, `stop` and `ready` of a partly landed raft, `start` reusing a parked layer's branch and PR) and c0249's rank (`rank:`, `next`'s order, the list order). Decisions it relies on (quoted for z-raft): Q1 "They merge now", Q3 "Wait, then block", Q5 "Agent on your word", Q6 "Wait a bit, then switch", Q8 "You re-approve", the prep decisions "resolve carries it" and "Blocked column first" (2026-11-13), "Do all three in this prep" (2026-11-17), and R0093's "go wwith 1 first then" (2026-11-19), which replaces Q7 "Keep one raft".

**Where c0250 sits (re-prep of 2026-11-19).** c0250 is layer 5 of R0093: c0248, c0300, c0256, c0247, **c0250**, c0260, c0262 (**Guess (prep) G1**, from R0093's F4 and F5 option (a)). Its in-raft dependencies, c0248 and c0256, are layers 1 and 3; it needs nothing of c0247, c0260 or c0262. c0260 and c0262 are re-prepared after it and block through `./zn block` and `./zn resolve` (the interface below), not through an item's `questions.md`. c0263 stays a cross-raft dependency (active in R0099), so `./zn ready R0093` waits for R0099's `done`. c0248's re-prep (merged 2026-11-19, PR #668) depends on d0331, so R0093 also waits for d0331's raft; and R0093 is readied without `layers: reviewed`, so it lands whole (c0248 outcome 9: `done --through` and `trace --through` refuse it). R0093 is built by an engine without c0250 (c0250's commands reach `main` only when R0093 lands), so a blocked layer of R0093 itself is resolved in place, or the raft is stopped (`./zn stop R0093`), its member re-prepared and the raft readied again, as c0248 outcome 9 and R0093's "Before the first layer" step 3 say (design review 007 F2); `./zn block` and `./zn resolve` serve the rafts readied after R0093 lands. c0250's helpers in `main.luau` go into c0248's `H` table, as c0248's interface says.

**c0256 stays as it is designed** (R0093 F3; c0256 is approved and is not re-prepared). Every case c0256's sequestered specs pin stays green on the top layer, as written: a dispatched step on an existing item that leaves `questions.md` is still c0256's question stop, answered by `./zn dispatch retry <id> --answer | --answer-file` or by an edited file, with the exchange as c0256 builds it; `dispatch new` and `retry new` are untouched; the zz-rules bullet **Questions and answers** (c0256), the README sentence and the help line c0256 appends stay whole. What c0250 changes is what every step is told to do on an item (block), and what a blocked item accepts (a resolve, not an answer flag). For that path only, this leaves partly undone two clauses of "resolve carries it" ("`dispatch retry` only resumes" and "c0256's local answer path stays only for a capture"), the captured Solution line "Replaces `questions.md` in c0117's design" and the captured Problem's "c0117 only writes a local … `questions.md`, which another host cannot see": the path stays for an item too, though no skill or prompt sends a step on an item down it. That is the owner's call (`## Open to the human`, F4).

**1. The blocked state.**
- `blocked` joins the closed status list (`status.NAMES`) and is stamped like the others (`blocked-<three words>`). Four edges join `status.ALLOWED`: `preparing>blocked` (an issue in design, or a draft raft in rafting), `active>blocked` (a readied raft; its members move with it), and `blocked>new` and `blocked>prepared`, which only `./zn resolve` takes (outcome 4). `./zn status <id> blocked` is refused ("only ./zn block blocks"), and so is `./zn status <id> <to>` from `blocked` ("only ./zn resolve unblocks").
- A blocked item's front matter carries `blocked: <reason>`. The reason is one of `review-exhausted`, `design-gap`, `needs-decision`, `red-gate`, `quota`, `tripwire` (`escalation.REASONS`, the one closed list). `resolve` removes the key.
- A blocked item holds no claim. No worker owns it, it needs no beat (c0265 never calls it lost), `./zn work next` and c0249's `next` never take it (it is not `prepared`), and an item that depends on it waits (its `depends_on` is not done). Its `rank:` line is never changed, so after the resolve it rejoins the stack where it was.

**2. The note: `escalation.md`.**
- The note lives in the blocked item's folder: the raft's folder for a raft, the issue's for an issue. It is published with the state in one commit. `z-nile/engine/escalation.luau` (new, pure) is its one reader and writer.
- Shape:
  ```
  # Escalation: R0120
  Item: R0120
  Reason: red-gate
  From: active
  Layer: c0230
  Actor: agent:claude-opus-5-5 effort high
  Session: 6f1c…
  Open: F2, F5
  When: 2026-11-20 03:10

  ## Question
  <one paragraph the human answers>

  ## What was tried
  <the attempts>

  ## Open findings or error
  <verbatim>

  ## Options
  - retry: <what it means here> (recommended)
  - amend-design: <what it means here>

  ## Resume
  ./zn resolve R0120 retry --answer "<your answer>"
  ./zn resolve R0120 amend-design --answer "<your answer>"
  ```
- The worker writes `## Question`, `## What was tried`, `## Open findings or error` and `## Options`. Each option is a bullet starting with one decision (outcome 4), and exactly one bullet ends with `(recommended)`.
- `./zn block` writes the header lines and `## Resume`. The header lines are `Item`, `Reason`, `From`, `Layer` for a readied raft (outcome 3; a draft raft has no layers, so its note has no `Layer:` line), `Actor` (the live actor, as c0263 reads it), `Session` (the running CLI session, as `sessionread` reads it, when one is known), `Open` (for `review-exhausted`, the ids of the unruled bullets under `## Open to the human` in the item's document and, on a raft, the Layer member's, as `openlist.pending` reads them) and `When` (UTC).
- `## Resume` has one line per decision the options name, each an exact `./zn resolve` command:
  - `split`'s line carries `--title "<the new issue's title>"`;
  - a `review-exhausted` note's lines carry one `--rule <Fn>="<your ruling>"` per open id;
  - a closing line says that an agent adds `--said "<the user's message>"`.
- It refuses a note that is missing a section, has an option naming no decision, does not have exactly one recommendation, or already holds a `## Resolution` ("this is the last block's note: write the new one").
- `resolve` appends `## Resolution`. When the same item blocks again, `block` first renames the resolved `escalation.md` to `escalation-NNN.md` (the next free number), so `escalation.md` is always the current block and every earlier one is kept.

**3. Blocking: `./zn block <id> <reason> [--layer <issue>]`.**
- Where it runs: the worker runs it in the item's worktree, after writing `escalation.md` in the item's folder there.
  - For an issue in design, that is the prep worktree.
  - For a draft raft being rafted, the rafting worktree.
  - For a readied raft, the raft's worktree.
- What it refuses:
  - an unknown reason;
  - an item that is neither `preparing` nor `active` on `origin/main`;
  - a note of the wrong shape;
  - the main checkout ("block runs where the note was written");
  - an issue that is a member of an active raft: "c0210 is in R0010, readied: block the raft: ./zn block R0010 <reason> --layer c0210";
  - a `--layer` that is not a member of the raft still in `active/`;
  - the reason `tripwire` in an agent session (`provenance.hint`): after a tripwire, the person checks the checkout and files the block (outcome 6).
- **The Layer** of a raft is `--layer`, which is required when two or more members are still in `active/` on `origin/main` (refused without it, exit 1, nothing published: `"<R> has c0210, c0220 still in active/: name the blocked layer: --layer <issue>"`); with one member left there, that member is the Layer (design review 004 F1). Only the step knows which layer needs the decision: under `./zn dispatch` nothing lands before a block, and on a raft without `layers: reviewed` nothing lands at all, so "the lowest member still in `active/`" would name a green layer below the blocked one. Every text that tells a step to block a raft gives `--layer <issue>` (the step prompt, the Headless paragraphs, z-work step 5, zz-execute's To escalate, zz-rules' `block` row). The Layer is never read from the current branch: after `done --through` the checkout sits on the lower layer, and before the first `start` it is detached.
- **Re-filing:** on an item that is already `blocked` but whose note is missing or does not parse on `origin/main`, `block` publishes the new note without moving the item (the recovery path; `audit` names it). The reason must equal the item's `blocked:` (a blocked item with no `blocked:` line takes the given reason), and a note on `origin/main` that does not parse is kept as `escalation-NNN.md`.
- One tracker commit on `origin/main`, `tracker: <id> blocked <reason>`:
  - an issue or a draft raft in `preparing`: status `blocked-…`, `blocked: <reason>`, and `escalation.md` added;
  - an `active` raft: the raft and every member still in `active/` move to the backlog stamped `blocked-…` with `blocked: <reason>`, with their `check.sh` paths rewritten back, as `./zn stop` moves them (its `moveOnOrigin`). A member already in `done/` stays there (c0248): the folder decides, since a landed member keeps the raft's claim stamp. `escalation.md` is added to the raft's folder. The raft's `prompt.md` and claim file are removed, and the main checkout is fast-forwarded, as `stop` does.
- It prints the parked branches and PRs, which are left as they are, as `stop` leaves them. It comments `BLOCKED: <reason>: <the question>` on the Layer's PR: it finds the Layer's branch with `layergit.layersOf` (unchanged) and runs `gh pr comment` on it. It skips the comment, with a warning, when the Layer has no PR yet, and a failed comment only warns (the PR is the visible record, zz-rules) and removes the worktree's copy of the note: main's copy is the note, and the next restack or sync brings it back.
- The green layers below the blocked one land before the block (Q1): c0248's `./zn done <R> --through <issue>`. z-work's worker runs it (outcome 6). Under `./zn dispatch` a step never runs `./zn done`: it blocks, and the dispatcher lands the layers below under c0252. After a tripwire nothing lands (outcome 6).

**4. Resolving: `./zn resolve <id> <decision> [--answer <text> | --answer-file <path>] [--said <text>] [--title <text>]`.**
- **Who** (Q5). Refused while `ZN_DISPATCH` or `ZN_HEADLESS` is set (c0253's headless loop sets `ZN_HEADLESS`, recorded on c0253): "resolve is the human's: a headless session is refused". Refused when the running CLI session is the note's `Session:`: an agent never resolves a block its own session filed. In an agent session (`provenance.hint(env).agent` with `ZN_DISPATCH` unset), `--said "<the user's message>"` is required, and it is recorded quoted as the user's word. A human in a terminal (no marker) needs none. No terminal test applies, because an interactive agent has no terminal. It runs in any checkout, the main one included, and publishes to `origin/main` itself.
- **Refused:** an item that is not `blocked` on `origin/main`; a decision outside the five; `split` without `--title`; `--answer` together with `--answer-file`; a `review-exhausted` resolve that leaves an id of the note's `Open:` without a `--rule <Fn>="<ruling>"`.
- **Rulings** (`review-exhausted`). `resolve` records each `--rule` in `## Resolution` (`Ruled F2: "<words>"`); in an agent session they are recorded as the user's word, with `--said`. It edits no document's open list: the list lives where it was written (a prep branch, a layer, the raft document). The next step runs `./zn rulings <id>` in its worktree, which writes `Ruled (user, <date>): <words>` under each bullet of the document's `## Open to the human` from the note's Resolution, and refuses a bullet with no recorded ruling. No agent writes a ruling of its own.
- **One tracker commit**, `tracker: <id> resolve <decision>`:
  - appends `## Resolution` to `escalation.md`: `Decision:`, `Answer:` (the text, or `none`), `By:` (c0263's live actor), `Said:` (the quoted words, in an agent session only) and `When:`;
  - removes `blocked:` and moves the status (table below);
  - appends c0263's `unblocked` row to the item's `provenance.md` (`provenance.record`, detail `decision=<d>` and, in an agent session, `said="<words>"`). It is the only row for this unblock: `resolve` never calls `status <id> new`, so c0282 adds none (c0282's Overlaps row);
  - leaves `rank:` as it is.

| decision | blocked from `preparing` (an issue or a draft raft) | blocked from `active` (a raft) |
|---|---|---|
| `retry` | `new`: its next design or rafting step reads the note with its resolution | `prepared`: the next `ready` resumes it at the blocked layer (c0248's `ready` skips landed members, and `start` reuses the parked layer's branch and PR) |
| `approve` | an issue: as `retry`, and the answer becomes a Decided line in the item's Problem; a draft raft: as `retry`, with the answer only in the Resolution | as `retry`, and the Decided line goes in the Problem of the member the note's `Layer:` names. That changes its approved contract, so `ready` refuses the raft until the user's own `./zn approve <member>` (Q8; #295's hash, c0283). `resolve` re-records that member's `grouped:` entry and every coherence review's `Grouped:` line for it, as compact and remap do (`keepRecords`): the change is the user's decision, so it gets no new raft-mode round |
| `amend-design` | an issue: `new` with `design: draft`, and z-design reads the note; a draft raft: as `retry` | the `Layer:` member leaves the raft (as `./zn unfold` takes it out) and goes to `new` with `design: draft`, with a copy of the note in its folder; the raft goes `prepared` with the rest |
| `split` | an issue: a new backlog issue of the item's type (as `./zn new`, `idea: unchallenged`), titled by `--title`, with the answer as its Problem; the item gains `Scope decision (user, <date>): "<the user's words>" (split into <new id>)` and then goes as `amend-design`. A draft raft: refused ("a draft raft has no design to split: resolve it amend-design, then split the issue in z-design") | the same on the `Layer:` member, which leaves the raft as in `amend-design` |
| `abort` | `new`: the claim is given back, as `status <id> new` | `prepared`, as z-stop leaves a raft; it prints the parked branches and PRs to close |

- **The Decided line's words** (Q5). In a terminal it quotes the answer: `Decided with the user (<date>), resolve approve: "<answer>"`. In an agent session it quotes `--said` and names the option: `Decided with the user (<date>), resolve approve: "<said>" (the option: <answer>)`. The line goes at the end of the document's `## Problem`; a document with no `## Problem` is refused, since the publish rule accepts the line only there.
- **A raft the Layer leaves.** When `amend-design` or `split` takes the Layer out and no unlanded member remains, the raft moves to `done/` if a member landed and to `retired/` if none did. Its whole folder moves to `<root>/rafts/done/<R>/` or `<root>/rafts/retired/<R>/` in the resolve's one commit, the only folder move a `blocked` or `resolve` commit may make. The moved `escalation.md` gains the resolution, and the moved `provenance.md` the `unblocked` row (only when the raft already has one: a moved folder gains no new file). The document loses `status:` and `blocked:`, and a retired raft gets `retired: emptied`. A member in `done/` is never touched by any decision.
- On a raft, the raft and every member it moved to the backlog carry `blocked:`, and a decision moves them together: each blocked member goes to `prepared` with the raft, except the `Layer:` member where its row says otherwise. The one `unblocked` row goes in the raft's `provenance.md`.
- The user's words in a `Scope decision` line are `--said` in an agent session and the answer in a terminal: only the user changes scope (z-design).
- After `retry`, `approve` or `amend-design`, the dispatcher's next run on the item re-runs the step with the note and its resolution (outcome 5).

**5. The dispatcher: an item's questions become its block** (prep Q1, "resolve carries it").
- The step prompt (`dispatch.prompt`) and the Headless paragraphs of z-design, z-raft, z-run and zz-execute say: "When a decision needs the user, write `escalation.md` in the item's folder and run `./zn block <id> <reason>`, then stop. Under `./zn dispatch`, do not run `./zn done`: the dispatcher lands the layers below (c0252)." Every step on an existing item is told to block instead of writing `questions.md`.
- **Review exhaustion is a block.** A finding still open when no further review round may run (a refuted finding or an unclosed high, left under `## Open to the human`) is the reason `review-exhausted`: z-design step 5.4, z-raft, zz-execute Phase 4 and Phase 5, the Headless paragraphs and `askText` say to write `escalation.md`, with the bullets verbatim under `## Open findings or error`, and run `./zn block <id> review-exhausted`. The wording names no number of rounds and does not say a second round is refused (**Guess (prep) G2**): today's one round reaches the cap after one round, and f0417's loops (5 idea, 9 design, 9 code rounds) reach it later, with the same sentence. `dispatch.next`'s open-list stop stays only as a fallback, and it names `./zn block`. After the resolve, the step runs `./zn rulings <id>` (outcome 4).
- **c0256's answer path stays beside the block** (R0093 F3; `## Open to the human` F4). A capture (`./zn dispatch new`, before any item exists) keeps c0256's local `questions.md` and `./zn dispatch retry new --answer`: there is no item to block yet. A step on an existing item that still leaves `questions.md` and does not block is c0256's question stop, unchanged: exit 3, "needs the user", the question copied into the exchange, answered by `retry <id> --answer | --answer-file` or by an edited file. No skill or prompt tells a step on an item to do that after c0250, so it is reached only by a step that does not follow them (c0256's fake CLIs do, and so would a model that ignored its prompt); its answer then stays in the main checkout's `.cache`, as c0256 keeps it.
- **A step that blocks and also leaves `questions.md`** (**Guess (prep) G3**): the block is its question. The dispatcher copies the note's `## Question` into the exchange (below), sets the `questions.md` aside unread as `questions-refused-N.md` (c0256's `freeName`, as c0256 sets aside a question it cannot take), and the stop names that file. Otherwise the exchange would hold two questions in a row, which `exchange.order` refuses, and the step would fail on a question nobody can answer.
- `dispatch.next` (pure) stops first, with `EXIT.user`, on an item that is `blocked` on `origin/main`: `"<id> is blocked (<reason>): ./zn resolve <id> <decision>"`, before the `questions` fact and every other state. The chain reads the item's state after every step, as it does for every other state.
- `./zn dispatch retry <id>`:
  - refused for a blocked item, with or without `--answer` or `--answer-file`, before anything moves: `"<id> is blocked: ./zn resolve <id> <decision> first"`. An answer flag never answers a blocked item: the answer is the resolution's;
  - after a resolve, it reruns the step, as it does today for a failed step. The exchange then ends in the resolution's answer, so a later `retry <id> --answer` is refused by c0256's own rule ("no question waits");
  - on an item that is not blocked, everything c0256 designs is unchanged.
- c0256's exchange keeps carrying the conversation into the re-run:
  - the dispatcher copies the note's `## Question` into the run's exchange as the question when the step blocks;
  - **the resolution reaches the next step on any host, once** (design review 003 F2, F3, F4). Wherever the dispatcher resumes an item whose `escalation.md` on `origin/main` holds a `## Resolution` this run has not carried (the chain, `./zn dispatch <id>`; `retry <id>`; a one-step run `./zn dispatch <step> <id>`, a nested review included), before any CLI starts and in this order: (a) when the exchange ends in a question that is not this note's (c0256's own question, still waiting from before the block), it closes it with c0250's own answer text `"(no reply: the item was blocked, and its resolution answers in the next message)"` (`escalation.SUPERSEDED`) and, when a `questions.md` waits, sets it aside unread as `questions-refused-N.md`, naming it: the resolution is the human's later decision, in git, and wins; (b) when the exchange does not end in this note's question (another host, a cleared `.cache`, or a block an interactive worker filed, which has no exchange), it adds the note's `## Question` as a question whose `step:` is the model step the item resumes with, never a script step: `z-run` for a raft blocked from `active`, `z-raft` for a draft raft, `z-design` for an issue (design review 004 F2); (c) it adds `escalation.answerText(resolution)` as the answer. The run state keeps two records with two keys (design review 004 F6): `st.blockQuestion`, the sha256 of `escalation.question(note)` when the note's question is copied (at the block, or by (b)), which the resolution's append does not change, so (a) and (b) compare the exchange's last question with it; and `st.carried`, the resolved note's blob sha when its resolution is carried, so a carried note is never added again (the note stays in the folder until the next block archives it).
  - **The re-run prompt after a carried resolution** (design review 004 F2): when the exchange's last two messages are the carried note's question and its resolution (the run state's records say so), `modelStep` hands `dispatch.prompt` `exchangeLastStep = exchangeAsker` for the step that resumes, so the step reads c0256's re-run form ("This is a re-run … The last file is an answer"), even when a script step (`z-ready`) ran between the resolve and the model step, or on a host with no history. For every other exchange c0256's rule is unchanged (its specs pin "a step that asked long ago, with something else run since, is not told it is a re-run").
  - **Once per run state, and not for an abort** (design review 005 F8). "Once" is per run state (`st.carried`): a host whose run state never carried the note carries it once more, which is the point of the any-host rule. The re-run prompt's override is keyed on `st.rerunCarried`, set when the carry writes the answer and cleared when the next model step starts, so only the first step after the carry reads the re-run form. A resolution whose decision is `abort` is never carried: the dispatcher records it as carried and adds nothing (the item went back to `new` or `prepared` because the human stopped it, and its next step starts fresh).
  - **The superseded question is crash-safe** (design review 005 F9): rule (a) writes the `SUPERSEDED` answer with c0256's `st.answering` (the sha256 of the waiting `questions.md`) in the same state save, as c0256's own retry does, so a dispatcher killed between the answer and the set-aside leaves a recorded half state the next run only finishes.
  - **An issue a blocked draft raft lists waits on it** (design review 004 F3). Under the dispatcher a draft raft is never the chain's id: the chain runs on an issue, and z-raft works on the raft `raft-plan` gave it. So `dispatch.Facts` for an issue gains `blockedBy: string?`: when the issue is not blocked itself and a raft that is `blocked` on `origin/main` lists it in `issues:` (the read `raft-plan` and `fold` make), `blocked` is that raft's reason and `blockedBy` its id. `next` stops first: `"<id> waits on <R>, which is blocked (<reason>): ./zn resolve <R> <decision>"` (exit 3); `retry <id>` is refused `"<R> is blocked: ./zn resolve <R> <decision> first"` and a one-step run starts nothing, as for the item itself; the block-time copy, the carry and its records read the raft's note, with `step: z-raft`. After `./zn resolve <R> retry` the raft is `new` again and no longer blocked, so `blockedBy` is nil; a third fact carries it (design review 005 F3): `Facts.resolvedBy: string?`, a raft that is not blocked, lists the issue in `issues:`, and whose `escalation.md` holds a `## Resolution` this run state has not carried. The carry and its records read that raft's note (`step: z-raft`), and the carry clears the issue run's last outcome (the old `z-raft` ok), so the chain does not stop on "rafted but its rafting PR is not open"; then the chain goes on as it does for a prepared issue (`raft-plan` returns that raft as `f.localRaft`, and z-raft claims it again). Neither fact names a raft for an issue in `done/`: a landed member a blocked raft still lists is done, and `./zn dispatch` on it says so as today. So c0256's prompt paragraph and its "no step starts with an open question" still hold.
  - Until the resolution is carried, `retry <id> --answer | --answer-file` on the resolved item is refused before anything moves: `"<id>: the resolution answered it: ./zn dispatch retry <id>"`. Afterwards c0256's own rule refuses a flag ("no question waits").
  - A one-step run (`./zn dispatch <step> <id>`, a nested `zz-review <id>` included) on a blocked item starts nothing: exit 3 with `dispatch.next`'s words, `"<id> is blocked (<reason>): ./zn resolve <id> <decision>"`, the exchange unchanged (c0256's one-step guard tests only `questions.md`, which a blocked item does not have).
  - A step that does not go through the dispatcher (an interactive z-work worker, a person's session) reads the note itself: z-design, z-raft, z-work and zz-execute say "When the item's folder holds `escalation.md` with a `## Resolution`, read it before you start: it is the human's decision on the last block." (docs.spec pins it). For `retry` the user's answer is only in the note, so this sentence is what carries it there. When it copies the resolution it also clears the run's last outcome, as `retry` does, so `dispatch.next` does not stop on the old step's ok outcome ("z-design ended but … still new"). The open-list fallback stop drops the ids the resolved note's `Ruled` lines cover, so it does not fire again before `./zn rulings` has run.
  - A nested step (a review) that needs the user says so in its review, and its stop message is `dispatch.nestedStop(id, raft)` (pure, design review 008 F1, F2; every place that prints the stop uses it), which tells its author to write `escalation.md` in the raft's folder for a layer of a readied raft and in the item's own folder otherwise ("… your author writes escalation.md in R0010's folder and runs ./zn block R0010 <reason> --layer c0050"; "… writes escalation.md in c0020's folder and runs ./zn block c0020 <reason>"), and to run the block command `dispatch.blockCommand(id, raft, "<reason>")` gives (design review 006 F3): `./zn block <id> <reason>` for an item that is not a member of an active raft, and `./zn block <R> <reason> --layer <id>` for an issue that is one (under c0248 a layer's review is dispatched with the issue's id), so the note goes in the raft's folder. The same function gives the command the open-list fallback stop and the step prompt name (`./zn block <R> <reason> --layer <issue>` for a raft id). `dispatch.resumeStep(f: Facts): string` (pure) gives the `step:` of a question the carry adds: `z-run` for a raft (readied or `prepared` after a resolve), `z-raft` for an issue with `blockedBy` or `resolvedBy`, `z-design` for any other issue (design review 006 F2). The message keeps c0256's words "only the step that started it can ask" (c0256's `step.spec` pins them) and no longer tells the author to write the reviewer's questions into its own `questions.md`.
- Quota: c0250 leaves the all-quota step as it is (it stops as today). The wait, and the block with `quota` past the cap, are c0253's, and c0253 reads the cap (outcome 7).

**6. z-work.**
- Step 5 is written onto f0399's text (landed 2026-11-17: guess mode) and c0248's, replacing only its tail "Then write `questions.md` in the raft folder … From the main checkout run `./zn stop <R>`.", so that f0399's first sentence and its last and c0248's pinned sentence ("`./zn done <R> --through <issue>` lands the green layers below it.") stay (design review 005 F1; **Guess (prep) G5**, pending `## Open to the human` F2): "5. A human decision is answered with a recorded guess (Guess mode, below) and the work goes on. Blocked means only: the same check failed after a real second attempt, a missing credential, or a choice that would drop or shrink a captured outcome (only the user changes scope). Then, if the raft carries `layers: reviewed` and layers below the blocked one are green, land them first with `./zn done <R> --through <issue>`. Write `escalation.md` in the raft folder, then run `./zn block <R> <reason> --layer <issue>` (the layer whose ticket needs the decision; `red-gate` for the failed check, `needs-decision` for the credential or the scope) in the raft's worktree. Tell the person, then run `./zn work next` again. Never narrow scope to get green." The pinned text ends at "… run `./zn work next` again.", where c0248 puts its sentence, then f0399's "Never narrow scope to get green." (pinned on its own); `./zn work next` names no raft on purpose: the blocked raft is no longer the session's. So in guess mode the capture's wall "an ambiguity only the human can settle" is a recorded guess, as f0399 rules for every human decision, and `needs-decision` blocks it only under `./zn dispatch`, where nothing is guessed; zz-execute's `review-exhausted` sentence is scoped the same way ("Under `./zn dispatch`, …; in guess mode, outside the dispatcher, each open bullet gets a `Guessed` line instead"). Every wall the capture names still has its reason. No skill tells a worker to write the raft-folder `questions.md` any more, but the signal is not retired: a raft that holds one still stops as today (`RaftFact.questions` stays; lesson zz-arch/retired-signals-fail-loud), so f0399's promoted `pick.spec` and the sequestered specs of c0306, d0295, c0267, f0417, c0249, c0254 and c0262 that build the field stay as they are.
- A raft readied without c0248's `layers: reviewed` marker (a raft readied before c0248's marker reached `main`; c0248 and c0250 land together, in R0093, so after it every raft `ready` readies carries the marker) lands whole: c0248's `done` refuses `--through` on it, so a block there lands nothing first and parks every layer; the same rule is in zz-execute's To escalate (c0248 outcome 9). R0093 itself never meets `./zn block`: it is built before c0250 is on `main` (Where c0250 sits).
- Step 5 also says: "Under `./zn dispatch` (the headless run step is this skill), do not run `./zn done`: the dispatcher lands the layers below (c0252)." zz-execute and zz-rules say the same (AC12).
- After a tripwire (a `REPOSITORY CHANGED` stop, a refused fixture identity), the worker writes `escalation.md` and runs neither `done --through` nor `block`. It tells the person, who checks the checkout and runs `./zn block <R> tripwire`. zz-execute and zz-rules say the same.
- An agent runs `./zn resolve` only when the user's message in this conversation tells it to. It quotes that message in `--said`, and never resolves a block its own session filed. z-work, zz-execute and zz-rules say so.
- `work.luau`, `workread.luau`, `readyfacts.luau` and `readycheck.luau` read the `blocked` status beside the `questions` fact, which stays (design review 003 F1):
  - a blocked raft is not claimable (`work.claimable`) and is never offered as a fix (`work.fixable` and `readyOn` already require `status == "prepared"`, which a blocked raft is not, so they need no change), and `whyNone` says `"<R>: is blocked (<reason>): a human resolves it with ./zn resolve"`;
  - `forRaft` of a blocked raft ends the session's hold (`"<R> is blocked: start a fresh session"`);
  - `readycheck.reason` refuses it first, keyed on its status (`"<R> is blocked: ./zn resolve <R> <decision> first"`), before "only a prepared raft is readied" and before the `questions` refusal;
  - #330's `--released` count counts a block.
- Step 10's "A blocked status is c0250 (`questions.md` is the only block signal)" goes.

**7. Quota.** `quota` is one of the reasons. `.models.toml`'s `[dispatch]` gains `quota_cap_hours = <whole hours, at least 1>`: `models.quotaCapHours(layers: { Layer }): number?` returns nil when no layer sets it, and a non-integer or a value under 1 is refused, naming the key. zz-rules and the README say that c0253's worker blocks with `quota` when every CLI stays out past it. The key's own comment in `.models.toml` says the same.

**8. The board and the lists** (prep Q2, "Blocked column first").
- `boardview.COLUMNS` becomes `{ "blocked", "ticket", "design", "raft", "ready", "run", "done" }`, and `boardview.column("blocked", _)` is `"blocked"`.
- A blocked card shows its reason and the note's `## Question` (its first 200 characters). The members of a blocked raft join the column with the raft's reason and question. `board.collect` finds them by the raft's `issues:` as well as each member's `raft:`, since a draft raft's members have an empty `raft:` on `origin/main` until the rafting PR lands.
- A blocked raft keeps its members in `issues:`. `raft-plan` skips, and `fold` refuses, an issue that a blocked raft lists, naming the raft. `board.collect` reads them with `escalation.parse`; a note that does not parse goes to `model.problems`. The column is banded like the others.
- `./zn list` and `./zn status` (with no target) print blocked items first, then in the order they print today. Once c0249 lands, its order also puts blocked items first.

**9. The documents say it.**
- zz-rules: Statuses, with `blocked`, its edges and `blocked:`; the `block` and `resolve` rows; Dispatch, where a step on an item blocks instead of writing `questions.md`, and `dispatch retry` on a blocked item. c0256's bullet **Questions and answers** (c0256) stays whole (c0256's `check.sh` greps it); c0250's bullet **A step on an item blocks it** follows it and says that a step that still writes `questions.md` on an item is answered as c0256's bullet says.
- The Headless paragraphs of z-design, z-raft, z-run and zz-execute. z-ticket's capture keeps `questions.md`.
- z-work, steps 5 and 10; z-stop (abort through `resolve`); zz-review (a nested reviewer's question).
- The raft prompt (`z-nile/templates/prompt.md`), after c0248's sentence "If a layer blocks, the layers below it land with `./zn done {{RAFT_ID}} --through <issue>`." (design review 005 F7): "Under `./zn dispatch` do not run `./zn done`: write `escalation.md` and run `./zn block {{RAFT_ID}} <reason> --layer <issue>`; the dispatcher lands the layers below (c0252)." (pinned by docs.spec; told to c0248's prep in the lead's report, in case c0248 prefers to own the sentence).
- The README:
  - Escalation to the human is `*exists* (c0250)`;
  - the `quota` row says "every CLI stayed out of quota past `quota_cap_hours`";
  - "takes the next unblocked item" becomes "takes the next raft that does not depend on the blocked one";
  - the dispatcher bullet says it "stops at a merge gate, at a blocked item, at a step's `questions.md` and at a failure" (a capture's `questions.md`, and c0256's path, still stop it), and the note's bullet says a step on an item blocks instead of writing c0117's local `questions.md`;
  - c0256's sentence on the dispatcher bullet (`./zn dispatch retry <id> --answer <text>`) stays as it is;
  - the Roadmap row for c0250 is `exists`.

**10. Audit.** `./zn audit` reports an error for:
- a `blocked` item without `blocked:`, or without an unresolved note that parses;
- `blocked:` on an item that is not blocked;
- a reason outside the list.

Each error names the command that clears it (`./zn block <id> <reason>` re-files a note, outcome 3).

**11. The interface the layers above build on** (R0093 F4, F5; for c0260's and c0262's re-preps and for f0417, which quote it; **Guess (prep) G4**). c0250 depends on nothing of c0247, c0260, c0262 or f0417, and this is all they need of it. Every command, reason, decision, exit code, fact and publish rule below is pinned by a c0250 spec, so it lands as written; the two publish builders and their types are named for f0417 and pinned by no spec (the specs reach them only through the commands).
- **Blocking**, a command: `./zn block <id> <reason> [--layer <issue>]`.
  - `--layer <issue>` is required for a raft with two or more members still in `active/` (Design 3). `<id>` is an issue or raft that is `preparing` on `origin/main` (a step that has not claimed its item yet claims it first, `./zn status <id> preparing`, as every design step does), or a raft that is `active`; an issue inside an active raft is blocked through its raft, `./zn block <R> <reason> --layer <issue>`. `<reason>` is one of `escalation.REASONS`. Run in the item's worktree (never the main checkout), after the caller wrote `<item folder>/escalation.md` with `## Question`, `## What was tried`, `## Open findings or error` and `## Options` (each option a bullet starting with one decision of `escalation.DECISIONS`, exactly one ending `(recommended)`). The item folder is the raft's for a raft (`<root>/rafts/active/<R>/` in a readied raft's worktree) and the issue's for an issue.
  - Exit 0: one tracker commit on `origin/main` (`tracker: <id> blocked <reason>`), the main checkout fast-forwarded, the parked branches and PRs printed on stdout, the worktree's copy of the note removed. Exit 1: refused, with a line naming the rule and the way past it (zz-arch rule 8); nothing is published. There is no other exit code.
  - After it, `./zn status <id>` prints `blocked`, the item's front matter carries `blocked: <reason>`, and `<item folder>/escalation.md` on `origin/main` holds the header lines `Item`, `Reason`, `From`, `Layer` (a raft), `Actor`, `Session` (when known), `Open` (`review-exhausted`) and `When`, and `## Resume`.
- **Resolving**, the human's command: `./zn resolve <id> <decision> [--answer <text> | --answer-file <path>] [--said <text>] [--title <text>] [--rule <Fn>=<ruling>]...`; refused (exit 1) under `ZN_DISPATCH` or `ZN_HEADLESS`, by the session the note's `Session:` names, and in an agent session without `--said`. Exit 0: one tracker commit (`tracker: <id> resolve <decision>`), the item `new` or `prepared` as the decision table says, `## Resolution` appended to the note (`Decision:`, `Answer:`, `By:`, `Said:` in an agent session, `Ruled Fn:` lines, `When:`). `./zn rulings <id>` (exit 0 or 1) writes the `Ruled (user, <date>)` lines under the item document's open bullets in the worktree it runs in.
- **The reasons** (`escalation.REASONS`, in this order): `review-exhausted` (a finding still open when no further review round may run), `design-gap`, `needs-decision`, `red-gate`, `quota`, `tripwire`. **The decisions** (`escalation.DECISIONS`): `amend-design`, `approve`, `split`, `retry`, `abort`. No later ticket adds a reason or a decision without changing this list and c0250's promoted specs: f0417's last gate uses only these six.
- **The pure functions a later command composes** (`z-nile/engine/escalation.luau`, the Public surface below): `parse`, `check`, `stamp`, `resolution`, `plan(from, isRaft, decision)`, `question`, `answerText`, `decidedLine`. A command that blocks and resolves in one publish (f0417's `./zn refuse`) builds its edits from these and from the two builders in `main.luau` that `cmd.block` and `cmd.resolve` call inside their `publish.commit`: `esc.blockEdits(paths, read, a: esc.BlockArgs): (esc.Edits?, string?)` and `esc.resolveEdits(paths, read, a: esc.ResolveArgs): (esc.Edits?, string?)`, each pure over the `paths` and `read` it is handed (the `publish.commit` callback's), returning the files to write or the refusal. `cmd.block` and `cmd.resolve` are their only callers in c0250.
  - The types: `esc.BlockArgs = { id: string, reason: string, layer: string?, note: string, actor: string, session: string?, when: string }` (`note` the text as the worker wrote it); `esc.ResolveArgs = { id: string, decision: string, answer: string?, said: string?, title: string?, rules: { [string]: string }, actor: string, when: string, newId: string? }` (`newId` the issue `split` makes, numbered by the command before the build); `esc.Edits = { writes: { [string]: string }, moves: { { from: string, to: string } }, subject: string }`.
  - The builders refuse only on what `read` shows them (design review 005 F6). `blockEdits`: an unknown reason; an item that is neither `preparing` nor `active` in that tree, or `blocked` with a note that parses (the re-file is accepted only for a `blocked` item whose note is missing or unreadable, and its reason must equal the item's `blocked:`); an issue that is a member of an active raft ("block the raft: `./zn block <R> <reason> --layer <issue>`"); a `--layer` on an issue or a draft raft, or one that is not a member still in `active/`; a missing `--layer` with two or more members in `active/`; a note of the wrong shape or one that holds a `## Resolution`. `resolveEdits`: an item that is not `blocked` in that tree; a decision outside the five or refused from that origin (`split` on a draft raft); `split` without a title; a missing or extra `--rule` for the note's `Open:`. The refusals that depend on the caller are `cmd.block`'s and `cmd.resolve`'s: the main checkout, `tripwire` in an agent session, `ZN_DISPATCH`/`ZN_HEADLESS`, the filing session, `--said` in an agent session, both answer flags. So a caller can hand `resolveEdits` the tree `blockEdits` produced.
  - The side effects stay in the commands, and a composer repeats the ones it needs: `cmd.block` removes the worktree's copy of the note, the raft's `prompt.md` and claim file (`.cache/tracker-claim-<R>`), fast-forwards the main checkout, prints the parked branches and PRs and comments `BLOCKED: …` on the Layer's PR; `cmd.resolve` numbers a `split`'s new issue (the counter push) before its build, prints the parked branches and PRs on `abort`, and fast-forwards the main checkout.
  - `publish.commit` makes one commit per call (`publish.luau`): a block and its resolve are two commits, made by two `publish.commit` calls in order (or by an API a later ticket adds). c0250 adds no two-commit publish.
- **The publish rule** a `blocked` or `resolve` commit passes (`publish.commit`'s fifth argument, the Public surface's `publish.luau` line), which a later ticket's writes in such a commit must also pass: every line of the origin text kept in order; added body lines only Decided and Scope decision lines inside `## Problem`; front-matter keys the item may change: `status:`, `blocked:`, `design:`, `issues:`, `grouped:`, `retired:`, `layers:`; a member: `status:`, `blocked:`, `design:`, `raft:`, `layers:`; a coherence review only its `Grouped:` lines; `escalation.md` created (it must parse) or appended by one `## Resolution`, an archive `escalation-NNN.md` never changed. A later ticket that writes anything else in such a commit (f0417's `idea: unchallenged`, its `### Message` under `## Ask (verbatim)`, its `- Loop (…)` line under `## Loops`) widens this rule and overrides the promoted `c0250/publish.spec` cases that pin it: "refuses any other added or changed line of the body" and "refuses a key the role may not change" (AC14).
- **Exit codes**: `block`, `resolve` and `rulings` exit 0 on success and 1 on every refusal (AC3 and AC5 pin `code == 1`); the dispatcher's stop on a blocked item is `EXIT.user` (3), pinned by AC8.
- **The facts `./zn work next` reads** (`work.luau`): `RaftFact.blocked: string?`, the raft's `blocked:` reason on `origin/main` (nil when it is not blocked), filled by `workread` from the raft's front matter. It joins `RaftFact.questions: boolean`, which stays with its source (the raft-folder `questions.md`) and meaning, so c0262's re-prep may keep or drop its use of it. A raft with `blocked` set is not claimable (`work.claimable`), is never a `fix` (`work.fixable`), `work.whyNone` says `"<R>: is blocked (<reason>): a human resolves it with ./zn resolve"`, `work.decide` on a named blocked raft is `{ action = "end", why = "<R> is blocked: start a fresh session …" }`, and `readycheck.reason` refuses it first, keyed on `status == "blocked"`: `"<R> is blocked: ./zn resolve <R> <decision> first"`. `readycheck.Raft.questions` stays; `readycheck.Raft` gains no field. A blocked *issue* is never in a `RaftFact`: an issue in design is not a raft, and a member blocks through its raft.
- **The dispatcher's facts** (`dispatch.Facts`): `blocked: string?` (the item's reason on `origin/main`, or that of a blocked raft whose `issues:` lists the issue; nil when neither) and `blockedBy: string?` (that raft's id) join, and `resolvedBy: string?` (a raft that is not blocked, lists the issue, and holds a resolution this run state has not carried; Design 5); `questions: boolean` stays (c0256's local file); `dispatch.next` stops on `blocked` before every other fact, with `EXIT.user` (3).
- **What the board shows** (`board.luau`): a blocked item's card in the column `blocked` with `reason` and `question` (the note's `## Question`, first 200 characters).

**The chore checklist.**
- **No behaviour change** for players: c0250 is tooling only. An item that never blocks moves, lists and dispatches exactly as today (the Regression guard's specs).
- **Quotes of c0250 in other items** (design review 004 F8; this prep edits no other item, so the lead sends these to their preps and records the sending in `harvest.md`): f0417's Dependencies line quotes the old definition of `review-exhausted` ("An unruled `## Open to the human` … is the reason `review-exhausted`"; c0250 now says "a finding still open when no further review round may run", G2), its `Overrides:` narrows `c0250/docs.spec` sentences that no longer need it and leaves out the two `c0250/publish.spec` cases its `refuse` and `resolve retry` writes (`idea:`, `### Message`, `- Loop`) would override (Section 11, the publish rule); c0247's parenthesis says a dispatched restatement moves to `escalation.md` once c0250 lands, while c0250 keeps a capture's `questions.md` (a capture has no item to block). f0417:188 blocks a member of an active raft by the issue's id (c0250 refuses that: `./zn block <R> <reason> --layer <issue>`) and names its resolve commit `tracker: <id> resolved <decision>` (c0250's subject is `tracker: <id> resolve <decision>`).
- **Existing work** on the day it lands. A raft folder holding z-work's `questions.md` on `origin/main` would no longer stop anything (an item stopped on a local `.cache/dispatch/<id>/questions.md` still is: c0256's path stays). There is none today: no `questions.md` is in `origin/main`'s tree. Implementation step 13's search must find none. If it finds one, the lead asks the user how to convert it, since z-work's stop leaves such a raft `prepared`, and `block` refuses a prepared raft.
- **Shared state:** none. `board.html` is generated, and the id counter is untouched.
- **Restated rules:** every skill paragraph that tells a step on an item to "write `questions.md`" changes (outcome 9), and the docs spec pins the new wording. The paragraphs that describe c0256's mechanism (its zz-rules bullet, its README sentence, its help line, z-ticket step 2) stay, because the mechanism stays.
- **Guards:** `publish.luau`'s new rule fails closed. A `blocked` or `resolve` commit may make only the edits the Public surface's `publish.luau` line lists, and anything else in it is refused as today.

**Public surface.**
- `z-nile/engine/escalation.luau` (new, pure):
  - `REASONS`, `DECISIONS`;
  - `parse(text: string): (Note?, string?)`;
  - `check(note: Note): string?`;
  - `stamp(text: string, header: Header): string` (the header and `## Resume`);
  - `resolution(text: string, r: Resolution): string`;
  - `plan(from: "preparing" | "active", isRaft: boolean, decision: string): Plan` (the table above: the status, `design: draft`, unfold, the Decided or Scope line, `regroup` for a raft's `approve`, and `refuse` for a decision refused from that origin; `plan("active", false, _)` is an error);
  - `rulings(note: Note): { [string]: string }` (the recorded `Ruled Fn` words);
  - `applyRulings(doc: string, note: Note, date: string): (string?, string?)` (the pure part of `./zn rulings`: the document with the `Ruled (user, <date>)` lines, or the refusal);
  - `decidedLine(date: string, decision: string, answer: string?, said: string?): string` and `scopeLine(date: string, words: string, newId: string): string`;
  - `answerText(r: Resolution): string` (the resolution as the exchange's answer);
  - `question(note: Note): string`;
  - in `dispatch.luau`, pure: `blockCommand(id: string, raft: string?, reason: string): string`, `nestedStop(id: string, raft: string?): string` and `resumeStep(f: Facts): string` (Design 5);
  - `SUPERSEDED`, the answer text that closes a c0256 question a resolution supersedes;
  - `nextArchive(names: { string }): string`;
  - the types `Header` (with `session` and `open`), `Note` (with `session` and `open`), `Resolution` (with `ruled`), `Option` and `Plan`.
- `z-nile/engine/status.luau`: `blocked` in `NAMES`, and the four edges.
- `z-nile/engine/main.luau`: `cmd.block`, `cmd.resolve`, `cmd.rulings` (`./zn rulings <id>`), the `status` refusals, `fold`'s refusal, and the `list` and `status` order; the publish builders `esc.blockEdits` and `esc.resolveEdits` (outcome 11) inside the `esc` table, kept as a field of c0248's `H` table (`H.esc`: c0248's interface says c0250 puts its helpers in `H` and declares no `H` of its own; the file is at Luau's limit of 200 top-level locals, so c0250 adds no top-level local; zz-arch lesson main-luau-local-limit), and `./zn --help` naming `block`, `resolve` and `rulings`.
- `z-nile/engine/audit.luau`: the blocked invariants (outcome 10).
- `z-nile/engine/raftplan.luau`: `raft-plan` skips a blocked raft's listed members; `rerecord(text, id, old, new): string` re-records a Layer member's `grouped:` entry, and a coherence review's `Grouped:` line, in `resolve approve`'s publish build (`keepRecords` itself works on the working tree).
- `z-nile/engine/dispatch.luau` and `dispatcher.luau`: `Facts.blocked`, `next`, `retry`'s refusal of a blocked item, the prompt, the exchange copy of the note and its resolution, the set-aside of a `questions.md` a blocking step also left, and the nested stop's text. c0256's item path (`questions.md`, `retry --answer`) is not changed.
- `z-nile/engine/work.luau`, `workread.luau`, `readyfacts.luau`, `readycheck.luau`: `RaftFact.blocked: string?` beside `RaftFact.questions` (which stays), `claimable`, `fixable`, `readyOn`, `whyNone`, `forRaft` and `decide` reading it; `readycheck.reason`'s first refusal keyed on the status (outcome 11).
- `z-nile/engine/board.luau`, `boardview.luau`, `board.html`: the column and the card.
- `z-nile/engine/models.luau`: `quota_cap_hours`.
- `z-nile/engine/publish.luau`: `publish.commit` takes a fifth argument, `escalation: boolean`, that marks a `blocked` or `resolve` commit. Only such a commit may create or append `escalation.md`, and move a resolved `escalation.md` unchanged to its archive name with the raft. Every line of the origin text is kept, in order. The only added lines it accepts are Decided and Scope decision lines inside `## Problem`, and front-matter changes by role. The item of the commit is the one whose `escalation.md` (or archive) it writes, and its members are the issues its document lists on `origin/main`. The item may change `status:`, `blocked:`, `design:`, `issues:`, `grouped:`, `retired:` and `layers:`; a member may change `status:`, `blocked:`, `design:`, `raft:` and `layers:`; no other document may change. A `resolve` that re-records a member's `grouped:` may also change the `Grouped:` lines of the raft's `design-review-NNN.md`, and nothing else in a review. A resolved or unreadable note moved to `escalation-NNN.md` is the only way a note is replaced; otherwise `escalation.md` is created (it must parse) or appended by one `## Resolution`, and an existing `escalation-NNN.md` is never changed. An emptied raft's folder moves to `done/` or `retired/` (outcome 4). Anything else in such a commit is refused, as today. Every other published-change rule is unchanged.

design.heading: Scalability
design.text: A block and a resolve are one published commit each, at human pace. The board reads one small note per blocked item. `dispatch.next` and `work.decide` gain one status test each, and no host keeps local state for a block.

design.heading: Maintainability
design.text:
- One closed reason list and one note reader (`escalation.luau`), used by `block`, `resolve`, the board, the dispatcher and z-work.
- One decision table (`escalation.plan`) maps each decision to its lifecycle edge, so a sixth decision is one row.
- The raft's move reuses `stop`'s `moveOnOrigin`, and the unblock row reuses c0263's `provenance.record`.
- z-work's raft-folder `questions.md` and the dispatcher's item `questions.md` stop being what any step is told to write: the block in git is the one signal a step on an item raises. The dispatcher's local file stays as c0256's mechanism (a capture's, and a step's that does not follow its prompt), with no second reader added for it.

design.heading: Usability
design.text:
- The board's first column is what waits on the person: the reason and the question, with the exact commands under `## Resume` in the note.
- A refusal names the command that gets past it (`./zn resolve <id> <decision>`).
- An agent asked to resolve has to quote the user's words, so the record says who decided.

extra.text:
### Checked
- AC1: `blocked` is a status with the edges `preparing>blocked`, `active>blocked`, `blocked>new` and `blocked>prepared`, stamped and parsed like the others; `./zn status` neither blocks nor unblocks.
- AC2: `escalation.luau` parses and checks a note (every section, every option naming a decision, exactly one recommendation), stamps its header and one resume command per option, keeps the reason list closed, and maps each decision from `preparing` and from `active` to its status and edits.
- AC3: `./zn block <issue> <reason>` on a `preparing` issue publishes one commit with the `blocked-…` status, `blocked: <reason>` and `escalation.md`, and refuses an unknown reason, a bad note, a note that already holds a resolution, the main checkout, a member of an active raft (naming its raft) and the reason `tripwire` in an agent session; on a blocked item whose note is missing it re-files the note without a move.
- AC4: `./zn block <R> <reason>` on an active raft moves it and its active members to the backlog blocked (a member in `done/` stays), adds the note to the raft's folder, removes the prompt and claim file, names the parked branches and PRs and comments on the open layer's PR; a second block keeps the resolved note as `escalation-NNN.md`; the Layer is `--layer`, required when two or more members are still in `active/`, or else the only member still there, never the current branch (after `done --through`, and from a detached worktree before `start`), a done `--layer` is refused, and the comment goes to the Layer's PR.
- AC5: `./zn resolve` is refused with `ZN_DISPATCH` set, requires `--said` in an agent session and records it quoted, requires none in a terminal, refuses `ZN_HEADLESS`, a resolve from the session that filed the block and an item that is not blocked, needs one `--rule` per open id of a `review-exhausted` note, and quotes `--said` in an agent session's Decided line.
- AC6: each decision moves the item as the table says, appends `## Resolution`, removes `blocked:`, appends exactly one `unblocked` row to `provenance.md` and keeps `rank:`; `amend-design` and `split` on a raft take the `Layer:` member out of the raft, and `split` makes a new backlog issue and a `Scope decision` line; `abort` on a raft leaves it `prepared` and names the parked branches and PRs; the rulings are recorded and `./zn rulings` writes them as `Ruled (user, …)` lines; a raft the Layer leaves empty moves to `done/` or `retired/`; on a draft raft `approve` and `amend-design` act as `retry` and `split` is refused.
- AC7: `approve` on a raft writes the Decided line in the `Layer:` member, and `ready` refuses until that member is approved again; `retry` makes the raft `prepared`, and `ready` and `start` resume at the blocked layer on its parked branch; `resolve approve` re-records the member's `grouped:` so that `ready` passes after the user's approve; a raft with a landed member resumes at layer 2 and leaves the done member byte for byte unchanged.
- AC8: a dispatched step that blocks stops the chain with exit 3 naming `resolve`; `dispatch.next` stops first on a blocked item; `dispatch retry` is refused while blocked, with or without an answer flag, and after the resolve the re-run step's exchange holds the question and the resolution as its answer; c0256's answer path stays beside the block for a capture and for an item whose step wrote `questions.md`; a finding still open at the round cap blocks with `review-exhausted`; a step that blocks and also leaves `questions.md` has the file set aside unread; `./zn dispatch <id>` after a resolve carries the resolution, on a host that never saw the block too, once; a one-step run on a blocked item starts nothing and one after the resolve carries it; a c0256 question still waiting at the resume is set aside and the resolution is its answer; an issue a blocked draft raft lists waits on the raft, and its next step carries the raft's resolution once; a resolved raft's z-run is told the resolution answers its own question; a review of a readied raft's layer that needs the user tells its author to block the raft, in the raft's folder; a dispatched z-run step blocks an active raft.
- AC9: a blocked raft is not claimable, `whyNone` and `forRaft` say so, and `readycheck` refuses it.
- AC10: the board's first column is `blocked`, each card with its reason and question; `./zn list` and `./zn status` print blocked items first; a blocked raft's members are found by its `issues:`, `raft-plan` skips them and `fold` refuses them.
- AC11: `quota_cap_hours` is read from `.models.toml`, and a value that is not a whole number of at least 1 is refused, naming the key.
- AC12: zz-rules, the Headless paragraphs, z-work, z-stop, zz-review and the README say block and resolve (c0256's bullet, sentence and help line kept whole beside them), `review-exhausted` is a finding still open when no further review round may run, the quota row says the cap, and the README's next item is the next raft; zz-execute, z-work and zz-rules say who files a tripwire block, that a dispatched step never runs `./zn done`, and when an agent may resolve.
- AC13: the fast specs this change touches still pass: `c0068/stop`, `c0117/dispatch`, `c0118/model`, `f0399/pick`, `f0399/docs`, and the tooling `work`, `readycheck` and `approve`, those of them not in `tests/slow.tsv` when it runs (the slow tier is the gate's, run by Implementation step 13).
- AC14: the publish rule for a `blocked` or `resolve` commit accepts only its listed edits and refuses an edited Scope line, a removed Decided line, a Decided line outside the Problem, `raft:` changed on a non-member, a rewritten `escalation-NNN.md` and an edited note body.
- AC15: `./zn audit` reports a `blocked` item without `blocked:` or a readable unresolved note, `blocked:` on an item that is not blocked, and a reason outside the list, each naming the command that clears it.
